==English== {{wp}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alter|en|companie||obsolete}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂-}} From {{inh|en|enm|companye||a team; companionship}}, from {{der|en|fro|compaignie||companionship}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|compagnie}}), possibly from {{der|en|la-lat||*compania}}, but this word is not attested. {{cog|fro|compaignie}} is equivalent to {{cog|fro|compaignon}} (Modern French: {{m|fr|compagnon}}) + {{m|fro|-ie}}. More at {{m|en|companion}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|werod}}, {{m|ang|gefer}}, {{m|ang|getæl}}, and {{m|ang|hired}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|a=RP|/ˈkʌmp(ə)ni/}} *** {{audio|en|en-uk-company.ogg}} ** {{IPA|en|a=dialectal|/ˈkɒmp(ə)ni/}} * {{IPA|en|/ˈkʌmpəni/|a=US}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-company.ogg}} * {{rhymes|en|ʌmpni|ʌmpəni|s=2}} * {{hyphenation|en|com|pany}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # A [[team]]; a group of people who work together for a common purpose. #: {{ux|en|a '''company''' of knights}} ## A group of [[performing]] [[artist]]s who put on [[show]]s together. ##: {{ux|en|a '''company''' of actors}} ## {{lb|en|nautical|military}} The crew of a [[ship]]. ##: {{ux|en|a ship's '''company'''}} ## {{lb|en|military}} A unit of approximately sixty to one hundred and twenty soldiers, typically consisting of two or three [[platoon]]s and forming part of a [[battalion]]. ##: {{ux|en|the boys in '''Company''' C}} ##* {{RQ:Bindloss Dust of Conflict|chapter=30|passage=It was by his order the shattered leading '''company''' flung itself into the houses when the Sin Verguenza were met by an enfilading volley as they reeled into the calle.}} ## A unit of [[firefighter]]s and their equipment. ##: {{ux|en|It took six '''companies''' to [[put out]] the fire.}} ## {{lb|en|espionage|informal}} An intelligence service. ##: {{ux|en|As he had worked for the CIA for over 30 years, he would soon take retirement from the '''company'''.}} ## {{lb|en|aviation|informal}} A specific [[aircraft]] or its [[airline]], usually used in air traffic communications to refer conveniently to another aircraft operated by the same airline. # A small group of birds or animals. # {{lb|en|legal}} An [[entity]] having [[legal]] [[personality]], and thus able to own [[property]] and to sue and be sued in its own name; a [[corporation]]. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:enterprise}} #: {{ux|en|a financial services '''company'''}} #* {{quote-book|en|author=[[w:Robert Barr (writer)|Robert Barr]]|title=Lord Stranleigh Abroad|chapter=4|url=http://openlibrary.org/works/OL1796924W |year=1913|passage=“{{...}} That woman is stark mad, Lord Stranleigh.{{...}}If she had her way, she’d ruin the '''company''' inside a year with her hare-brained schemes; love of the people, and that sort of guff.”}} ## {{lb|en|business}} Any [[business]], whether [[incorporated]] or not, that [[manufacture]]s or [[sell]]s [[product]]s (also known as [[goods]]), or provides [[services]] as a [[commercial]] [[venture]]. ##: {{ux|en|Marconi [[set up]] the '''company''' who made the first radios.}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|author=w:George Monbiot|volume=188|issue=23|page=19|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |title=Money just makes the rich suffer|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/may/06/politics-envy-keenest-rich|date=2013-05-17|passage=In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. {{...}} The public realm is privatised, the regulations restraining the ultra-wealthy and the '''companies''' they control are abandoned, and Edwardian levels of inequality are almost fetishised.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011071319/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/may/06/politics-envy-keenest-rich|archivedate=11 October 2026}} ##* {{RQ:Economist |title=Obama goes troll-hunting|url=http://www.economist.com/news/business/21579011-president-proposes-new-round-intellectual-property-reform-obama-goes-troll-hunting|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=95|passage=According to this saga of intellectual-property misanthropy, these creatures [patent trolls] roam the business world, buying up patents and then using them to demand extravagant payouts from '''companies''' they accuse of infringing them. Often, their victims pay up rather than face the costs of a legal battle.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629210715/http://www.economist.com/news/business/21579011-president-proposes-new-round-intellectual-property-reform-obama-goes-troll-hunting|archivedate=29 June 2017}} ##* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Jackie Wattles|title=Some Old Spice and Secret deodorants recalled after cancer-causing chemical is detected|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/11/26/business/old-spice-secret-deodorant-recall-benzene|date=2021-11-26|passage=The '''company''' added it has not “received any reports of adverse events,” but it’s moving forward with the recall out of “an abundance of caution.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260220151128/https://www.cnn.com/2021/11/26/business/old-spice-secret-deodorant-recall-benzene|archivedate=20 February 2026}} ## The members of a partnership business who are not listed in the company's name; unnamed individuals in an entourage or other group. ##: {{ux|en|Smith, Capitano and '''Company'''}} ##: {{ux|en|Here come Will, Martin and '''company'''.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[companionship|Companionship]]. #: {{ux|en|I treasure your '''company'''.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=I|page=2|passage=He used to drop into my chambers once in a while to smoke, and was first-rate '''company'''. When I gave a dinner there was generally a cover laid for him. I liked the man for his own sake, and even had he promised to turn out a celebrity it would have had no weight with me.}} ## {{lb|en|uncountable}} One or more social [[visitor]](s) or [[companion]](s). ##: {{ux|en|Keep the house clean; I have '''company''' coming.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|author=w:Charles Johnstone|title=The Reverie; or, A Flight to the Paradise of Fools|url=http://books.google.com.sg/books?id=1mAzAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA202|volume=2|location=Dublin|publisher=Printed by Dillon Chamberlaine|year=1762|page=202|oclc=519072825|passage=At length, one night, when the '''company''' by ſome accident broke up much ſooner than ordinary, ſo that the candles were not half burnt out, ſhe was not able to reſiſt the temptation, but reſolved to have them ſome way or other. Accordingly, as ſoon as the hurry was over, and the ſervants, as ſhe thought, all gone to ſleep, ſhe ſtole out of her bed, and went down ſtairs, naked to her ſhift as ſhe was, with a deſign to ſteal them {{...}}}} ##* {{RQ:Travers Cuckoo in the Nest|chapter=5|passage=The departure was not unduly prolonged. In the road Mr. Love and the driver favoured the '''company''' with a brief chanty running. “Got it?—No, I ain't, 'old on,—Got it? Got it?—No, 'old on sir.”}} ## {{lb|en|figurative}} One or more other person(s) who are nearby, are approaching, or are (e.g. covertly) watching, especially if they may have hostile intentions (like [[adversary|adversaries]] or [[rival]]s). ##: {{ux|en|Get your guns ready: intel said there'd be no hostiles in the area, but it looks like we've got '''company'''.}} ##: {{ux|en|I thought we'd be the only ones exploring this abandoned tunnel system today, but judging by that light up ahead, it looks like we've got '''company'''. ==English==

===Pronunciation===

* {{IPA|en|/ˈhɛv/|a=NZ}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:haven<id:have>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize}}
From {{inh|en|enm|haven}}, from {{inh|en|ang|habban|t=to have}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*habbjan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*habjaną|t=to have}}, durative of {{m|gem-pro|*habjaną|t=to lift, take up}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*kapyéti}}, an imperfective formation to the root {{m|ine-pro|*kap-|id=seize||to take, seize, catch}}. Related to {{m|en|heave}}.

Since there is no common Indo-European root for a transitive possessive verb ''have'' (notice that {{noncog|la|habeō}} is not etymologically related to English ''have''), Proto-Indo-European probably lacked the ''have'' structure. Instead, the third person forms of ''[[be]]'' were used, with the possessor in [[dative case]], compare Latin ''mihi est / sunt'', literally ''to me is / are''.<ref>[http://books.google.fi/books?id=XlJrPvrGfO0C&pg=PA22&lpg=PA22&dq=%22mihi+est%22+indo-european&source=bl&ots=nQ3y6cgbSp&sig=vpKTQ-OWYXv7dYG3_8RHn9uKYHY&hl=fi&ei=bC3yTP3PKojOswb6xPnyCg&sa=X&oi=book_result&ct=result&resnum=1&ved=0CBkQ6AEwAA#v=onepage&q=%22mihi%20est%22%20indo-european&f=false Internal Reconstruction in Indo-European: Methods, Results, and Problems]</ref>

The nonstandard {{senseno|en|to be an age|t=to be (an age)}} is a {{glossary|semantic loan}} from other languages’ term for {{m-g|to possess, own}}, such as {{semantic loan|en|fr|avoir|notext=1}}, {{semantic loan|en|pl|mieć|notext=1}}, and {{semantic loan|en|es|tener|notext=1}}.

{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|hae||to have}}, {{cog|frr|haa}}, {{m|frr|heewe||to have}}, {{cog|stq|häbe}}, {{m|stq|hääbe||to have}}, {{cog|fy|hawwe||to have}}, {{cog|af|hê||to have}}, {{cog|gsw|haa}}, {{m|gsw|heen}}, {{m|gsw|hoh}}, {{m|gsw|hä}}, {{m|gsw|häbä}}, {{m|gsw|hè||to have}}, {{cog|bar|hobm}}, {{m|bar|hobn}}, {{m|bar|hoom}}, {{m|bar|håbn||to have}}, {{cog|cim|haban}}, {{m|cim|hen}}, {{m|cim|håm||to have}}, {{cog|nl,nds|hebben||to have}}, {{cog|de|haben||to have}}, {{cog|li|haane}}, {{m|li|höbbe||to have}}, {{cog|lb|hunn||to have}}, {{cog|mhn|hom||to have}}, {{cog|wym|hon||to have}}, {{cog|yi|האָבן||to have}}, {{cog|da|have||to have}}, {{cog|ovd|åvå||to have}}, {{cog|fo|hava||to have}}, {{cog|is|hafa||to have}}, {{cog|nb|ha||to have}}, {{cog|nn|ha}}, {{m|nn|hava}}, {{m|nn|have}}, {{m|nn|hå||to have}}, {{cog|sv|ha}}, {{m|sv|hafva}}, {{m|sv|hava||to have}}, {{cog|got|𐌷𐌰𐌱𐌰𐌽||to have}}, {{cog|sq|kap||to grab, catch, grip}},<ref>{{R:sq:Orel:1998|kap|page=169}}</ref><ref>{{R:sq:Demiraj|head=kap}}</ref> {{cog|la|capiō||take|pos=verb}}, {{cog|ru|хапать||to seize}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|haue||alternative typography|obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|hae||Scottish-English}}
* {{l|en|hav}} (May be used by advocates of {{w|English spelling reform}}.)

====Verb====
{{en-verb|has|having|had}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[possess]], [[own]].<ref>{{R:OneLook}}</ref>
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' a house and a car.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[hold]], as something at someone's [[disposal]].
#: {{ux|en|Look what I '''have''' here—a frog I found on the street!}}
#: {{ux|en|Do you '''have''' the key?}} (not necessarily one's own key)
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To include as a part, ingredient, or feature.
#: {{ux|en|The stove '''has''' a handle. The shirt '''has''' sleeves.}}
#: {{ux|en|The words ''cow'' and ''dog'' '''have''' three letters.}}
#: {{ux|en|A government '''has''' three branches: the executive, legislative, and judicial.}}
#: {{ux|en|The movie '''has''' lots of action.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} {{n-g|Used to state the existence or presence of someone in a specified relationship with the subject}}.
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' two sisters.}}
#: {{ux|en|She doesn’t '''have''' any friends.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' a really mean boss.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[consume]] or [[use up]] (a particular [[substance]] or [[resource]], especially [[food]] or [[drink]]).
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' breakfast at six o'clock.}}
#: {{ux|en|You've already '''had''' five drinks!}}
#: {{ux|en|She's '''had''' more than enough time already.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[undertake]] or [[perform]] (an action or activity).
#: {{ux|en|Can I '''have''' a look at that?}}
#: {{ux|en|He's '''having''' a tantrum about it.}}
#: {{ux|en|I’m going to '''have''' a bath now.}}
#: {{ux|en|Let’s '''have''' a game of tiddlywinks.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[schedule]]d to [[attend]], [[undertake]] or [[participate]] in.
#: {{ux|en|What class do you '''have''' right now? I '''have''' English.}}
#: {{ux|en|Fred won’t be able to come to the party; he '''has''' a meeting that day.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' a lot of work to do.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[experience]], [[go through]], [[undergo]].
#: {{ux|en|We '''had''' a hard year last year, with the locust swarms and all that.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''had''' surgery on his hip yesterday.}}
#: {{ux|en|I’m '''having''' the time of my life!}}
#: {{ux|en|I hope you '''have''' a wonderful birthday.}}
#: {{ux|en|This year we're '''having''' Christmas with my wife's family in Thunder Bay.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[afflict]]ed with, [[suffer]] from.
#: {{ux|en|He '''had''' a cold last week.}}
# {{sid|en|perfect}} {{lb|en|auxiliary verb, taking a [[past participle]]}} {{n-g|Used in forming the [[w:Perfect aspect|perfect aspect]].}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' already eaten today.}}
#: {{ux|en|Mom''''s''' gone real mad, she '''has'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|The universe is expanding and '''has''' been since its beginning.}}
#: {{ux|en|I will '''have''' left by the time you get here.}}
#: {{ux|en|This is the first (and last) time I''''ve''' eaten lobster.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'''’ve''' worked here for exactly four years, one month and 10 days.}}
#: {{ux|en|The dogs '''have''' eaten your dinner, and I ate the last of the frozen burgers this morning.}}
#: {{ux|en|Uncle José '''has''' crashed the car again. He ran into a tree.}}
#: {{ux|en|The American Revolution '''has''' influenced every democratic process in Europe since the 19th c.}}
#: {{ux|en|I'm [[going to]] [[take a bath]] after I''''ve''' answered these emails.}}
# {{n-g|Used as an interrogative verb before a [[pronoun]] to form a [[tag question]], echoing a previous use of 'have' as an auxiliary verb or, in certain cases, main verb. (For further discussion, see the appendix [[Appendix:English tag questions|English tag questions]].)}}
#: {{ux|en|They haven’t eaten dinner yet, '''have they'''?}}
#: {{ux|en|Your wife hasn’t been reading that nonsense, '''has she'''?}}
#: {{ux|en|He has some money, '''hasn’t he'''?}}
# {{lb|en|auxiliary verb, taking a [[w:Infinitive|to-infinitive]]}} ''See'' '''[[have to]]'''.
#: {{ux|en|I '''have''' to go.}}
# {{senseid|en|give birth}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[give birth]] to.
#: {{ux|en|The couple always wanted to '''have''' children.}}
#: {{ux|en|My wife is '''having''' the baby right now!}}
#: {{ux|en|My mother '''had''' me when she was 25.}}

=====Usage notes=====
In certain dialects, expressions (e.g., ''I '''have'''n't the [[faintest]] idea'') , and literary use, the lexical ''have'' can be used without ''do''-support, meaning the sentence ''Do you have an idea?'' can also be ''Have you an idea?'' This makes ''have'' the only lexical verb in Modern English that can function without it, aside from some [[nonce]] examples with other verbs in set phrases, as in ''[[what say you|What say you?]]'', and aside from the verb {{m|en|be}} where this is considered lexical.

The auxiliary ''have'' which forms the perfect tense never uses ''do''-support, so ''Have you seen it?'' cannot be *''Do you have seen it?''.

A sentence can't end with a contracted form of ''have'' or ''has'', so the response to ''Have you done it?'' might be ''I have'' but not ''I've''; similarly, one might respond to ''Has he done it?''  with ''He has'' but not ''he's''. Also,  ''do'' or ''does'' cannot be followed by a contracted form of ''have'' or ''has''. It's possible to say or write ''I do have'' or ''She does have'' but not ''I do've'' or ''She does've''.

All modal verbs used to express certainty in the past take '''have''' + past participle: ''She must''''ve''' had a bad day – she looks terrible!''
